newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI T-BILL REPO RATES END DOWN, SPOTS UP.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI T-BILL REPO RATES END DOWN, SPOTS UP.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed lower across the board in slow trading on Wednesday with fund demand decreasing due to the poor performance of domestic A share markets, traders said.
A lack of new A share issues on Wedensday and Thursday was another factor depressing the demand, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 8.00 percent from 10.90 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover on the six-contract market plunged to 1.25 million lots from 4.25 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The domestic share indices on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges have fallen for the past few days on weak market sentiment.
Traders said the fall left institutions unwilling to borrow on the repo market, which has served as a reservoir for funds to the A share markets in recent years.
"The fall on the stock markets left the repo market without stimuli to boost trading and pushed down the rates,," one trader said.
Traders said they expected the contracts to see a technical rebound on Thursday after Wednesday's sharp losses.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly higher, led by the strong performance of the two long-term contracts of 10 years and seven years, traders said.

The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in July 2006 rose to 113.08 yuan from 112.42 yuan. The seven-year contract gained solidly to 101.05 yuan from 100.19. They were supported by their high yields, traders said.
Combined volume on the eight-contract market rose to 995,792 lots from 530,565 lots.
Traders said the spot contracts would see a correction on Thursday after the sharp rises of the past two days.
